title: Accusative 2: Feminine Things Change
description: Feminine nouns ending in -а or -я change to -у or -ю in the accusative.
descriptionRussian: Женские существительные, оканчивающиеся на -а или -я, меняются на -у или -ю в винительном падеже.
intro: Lesson 1 gave you the easy half: masculine things keep the same form in the accusative that they have in the dictionary. Feminine nouns are the other half, and these do change. It is one letter at the end of the word. Once you can recognize a feminine noun, you can build its accusative without stopping to think.
rules: Feminine nouns ending in -а change to -у in the accusative: книга → книгу, школа → школу, машина → машину.
Feminine nouns ending in -я change to -ю in the accusative: песня → песню, неделя → неделю, кухня → кухню.
examples: Маша читает книгу. (Masha is reading a book.) книга → книгу.
Я слушаю музыку. (I am listening to music.) музыка → музыку.
Антон любит школу. (Anton loves school.) школа → школу.
Мы пьём воду. (We are drinking water.) вода → воду.
Я слушаю песню. (I am listening to a song.) песня → песню.

items.hint: What is the nominative form? How does -а change in the accusative?
items.explanation: Книга is feminine ending in -а. The accusative swaps -а for -у: книгу.

items.hint: Музыка is feminine. What's the rule for -а endings?
items.explanation: Музыка ends in -а. The -а consistently swaps to -у for feminine nouns: музыку.
Газета (newspaper) is feminine ending in -а. Accusative: -а → -у, so газету.

items.promptEnglish: What do you see? I see a house.
items.hint: Recap from lesson 1: дом is masculine inanimate. Does it change?
items.explanation: Recap: masculine inanimate nouns don't change in the accusative. Дом stays дом. Today's rule is for feminine nouns only.

items.promptEnglish: I am listening to a song.
items.hint: Песня ends in -я. What does -я become in the accusative?
items.explanation: Песня is feminine ending in -я. The accusative swaps -я for -ю: песню.

items.hint: Кухня ends in -я. Apply the rule.
items.explanation: Кухня (kitchen) is feminine ending in -я. Accusative: -я → -ю, so кухню.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Feminine nouns ending in -а change to -у in the accusative.

errorCorrection.explanation: Вода is feminine and ends in -а, so the accusative swaps -а → -у: воду. Вода in the sentence is the nominative form (the form you'd use if water were the subject: 'Вода льётся', 'water flows'). For the direct object, the -у ending is required.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я каждый день ем пицца на обед.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I eat pizza for lunch every day.
errorCorrection.explanation: Пицца is feminine in -а, so its accusative is пиццу, the standard -а → -у swap. Пицца as a direct object after есть always takes -у.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я очень люблю деревня моей бабушки.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I really love my grandmother's village.
errorCorrection.explanation: Деревня is feminine ending in -я, so the accusative swaps -я → -ю: деревню. The -я version of the rule is exactly parallel to the -а version: -а → -у, -я → -ю.

minimalPairs.explanation: Книга is the direct object of 'любит', so it must be in the accusative. Feminine -а changes to -у: книгу. Книга is the nominative (used when the noun is the subject, like 'Книга на столе').
Газета is feminine ending in -а. As the direct object, it takes the accusative form газету. Газета would be the nominative form ('Газета на столе').

reviewVocab.example: Книга, школа, песня — это женский род.
Окончание -а меняется на -у в винительном падеже.
